function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content: Use the platform’s “show” command (e.g., `show interface <name>` on Cisco IOS/IOS‑XE, `show interfaces terse` on Juniper Junos) or query the device via SNMP/RESTCONF/NETCONF to pull the interface’s operational state, statistics, and configuration details. For example, on a Cisco router you could run `show interface GigabitEthernet0/1` to see status, errors, and traffic counters, or use `show running-config interface GigabitEthernet0/1` to view its config. If you’re automating, you can call the device’s RESTCONF endpoint `/interfaces/interface/<name>` or use an SNMP walk on OIDs like `ifTable` to programmatically retrieve the same data.
